cohort: Parturient women undergoing category 2 and 3 cesarean deliveries at a tertiary perinatology center were enrolled.
finding: General and epidural anesthesia were associated with a shorter decision-to-delivery interval (DDI) compared to spinal anesthesia in category 2 and 3 cesarean deliveries, with general anesthesia also linked to higher maternal blood loss and postoperative complications but no significant differences in neonatal outcomes (Apgar, pH, base excess).
mod_finding: For category 2 and 3 cesarean deliveries, general and epidural anesthesia shortened the decision-to-delivery interval compared to spinal anesthesia, but general anesthesia led to increased maternal blood loss and postoperative complications.
gest_age: Included preterm births (before 32nd week and between 32nd and 37th week of pregnancy).
